intended_object: Given a family of spaces X, this takes a topological space Y that is X-generated and returns Y as an object of the category of X-generated spaces. The category is defined in this file as a full subcategory of TopCat. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
This is the standard `.of` constructor used for bundled categories. The file defines `GeneratedByTopCat X` as the full subcategory of `TopCat` cut out by the property `IsGeneratedBy X`. `of Y` packages two things: the bundled space `↧Y` (that is, `TopCat.of Y`) and the instance `IsGeneratedBy X Y` as the proof that Y belongs to the subcategory. So it is exactly Y regarded as an object of the category of X-generated spaces.

It works in the natural generality: any index type, any family of topological spaces X, and any universe for Y. It only bundles data and proofs, so there are no degenerate cases where it could go wrong. You could also argue it is just a bundling device rather than a mathematical object. Either way, it correctly represents the intended object, and it does not duplicate any more general Mathlib definition.
